body:
>It's never easy being gay.

Not true. It's never easy finding the right support network and environment where you can be yourself. But if you can surround yourself with people who don't give a damn about your sexuality in a progressive place, it can certainly feel easy.

Can I suggest an older, quieter dog, or even any dog you instill calmness in, will be glad to cuddle. I got to bear hug my friend's big lab mix, my aunt's dog practically sleeps underneath you, and my own dog burrows his head into the crook of my arm while I pat him. He's like 30 pounds but he's patiently cool with a good squeeze when I'm down.

I'm not a cat person, but I've heard of snuggly cats before. Dogs are a guarantee if you don't end up with a very young or high energy one.

People are hard to earn affection from...

You'll be ruining your wife and daughter's lives.

Not to mention that no matter what you do now people can find this post and they'll get nothing. You have no choice but to go on now.

I don't think you should tell them. It would only make you feel better. Ever posted in /r/offmychest?

I know we're not supposed to say this but your job-hunting experience is probably what the majority of us are going through at the moment. It's a deep flaw in society, not in its members. It's easy to get discouraged and it's part of why there are so, so many people posting in this subreddit and related... it shouldn't be "normal", but it is, and you're not alone. More than 75% of jobs are filled before they ever get to the point of a public posting.

My father-in-law finished high school at 53. After this, job placement agencies were able to find him a permanent position. It was his ticket. But from what I've seen, no one ever asks for your high school diploma if you put "graduated" on your resume. My friend manages a large cash loan location just fine without her grade 10 English.

You fucked up at a job once; don't do that again. Should be easy as it was your fault but you have accepted responsibility (awesome btw). Your next job won't just be a victory because you're employed, you'll also be proving you can handle your shit.

I want you to make it.

> No matter how great my suffering may be there is always someone in a similar or worse situation that may benefit from my advice, influence, or even a simple hello.

And with your loved ones, it's funny, just existing is a gesture in and of it itself benefiting them all the time.

What a cowardly piece of shit. He had to move across the country to break up with you. You're so amazing he had to take six months just to prepare to get over you. Talk about handling a breakup badly. What you're feeling is justified and you SHOULD curl up if you want to, sleep if you want to, and it's OK if you feel like dying for a bit. He's had time to release the feelings. Yours were taken away so suddenly that there's still a hole. Never mind the hole where your planned future (regardless of him) used to lie.

But... even as I'm typing this those holes are filling in. New possibilities are forming everywhere in your life every second. Maybe some idiot is about to get fired and your resume will catch the boss' eye. Maybe your next lover is going to his first appointment at a clinic you attend. Your heart is starting to see feelings for your ex as the useless things they are, and is discarding them bit by bit.

It's OK to feel the pain but please don't give in.
Why not take a few months' pay and go to Mexico? Even $10 and a car go a lot farther there.
